study type: Propensity score matched study (nested within a national cohort)
outcome: Neonatal intensive care unit admission for at least 24 hours
cohort: Term singleton babies without congenital anomalies (n=715,449, of whom 257,872 were included in the propensity-matched analysis)
finding: In a propensity-score matched analysis, intrapartum epidural analgesia was associated with an increased risk of low Apgar score and neonatal intensive care unit admission.
mod_finding: The association between intrapartum epidural analgesia and low Apgar score was higher in those who had a spontaneous start of labour or a spontaneous vaginal delivery.
